The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently upheld the government’s decision to deny an Indian visa to a US citizen convicted of a sexual offence [Dhanraj Rajendra Patel & Anr v. Union of India & Ors] . Justice Amit Mahajan said that the government was within its right to prevent such people from setting foot on Indian soil. “The issuance of a visa is a sovereign function of the State that is embedded in considerations of national security, foreign policy and administrative discretion. Petitioner No.1, admittedly, has been convicted as a sex offender in the United States of America and the respondents are within their rights to prevent such people from setting foot on Indian soil,” the Bench observed. The Court emphasised that when such dictates are issued against the individual choices of a citizen, it is the duty of the law-enforcing authority to take appropriate legal steps. " What dress one wears is ordinarily a matter of personal choice of every citizen of this country. No one or society as a whole can dictate how a citizen should dress without the backing of the law. This is a part of the fundamental rights of every citizen, " the Court said. It added that clothes are an expression of culture, comfort, and individual choice which cannot be used to measure a person's worth or dignity. In the suit, he also flagged that there are mobile apps available on Google Play Store that exploit his personality attributes without his consent. items.title: CJI Surya Kant to attend NLSIU convocation on October 17
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant will attend the 34th annual convocation of the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru on October 17. The convocation will be held from 11 am to 1 pm at the Jnana Jyoti Auditorium on Palace Road, Bengaluru. Justice Kant, who is the Chancellor of NLSIU, will preside over the ceremony, the University said in an invitation circulated to invitees. The convocation comes after NLSIU had earlier cancelled the ceremony scheduled for September 12 after issuing a notice announcing that no convocation would be held for the 2026 batch due to "unavoidable circumstances" and that students would be conferred their degrees in absentia. The cancellation came amid a controversy over the proposed presence of CJI Kant and Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra at the ceremony. More than 700 current students, graduating students and alumni had objected to their participation. The development followed a separate controversy at NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad, where students had opposed the proposed presence of CJI Kant at their convocation. The plea contends that prolonged vacancies have affected the functioning of these regulatory bodies and deprived electricity consumers of effective remedies against distribution companies. items.summary: The DSNLU Queer Alliance (DSQA) at Damodaram Sanjivayya National Law University (DSNLU), Visakhapatnam has received official recognition from the University days after a Constitutional Law faculty member made derogatory remarks on queer relationships. DSQA said that Vice-Chancellor (VC) Prof D Surya Prakasa Rao accepted all its demands at an October 8 meeting. A committee has also been set up to inquire into the incident. items.title: Supreme Court moots dedicated corpus to fund treatment for Spinal Muscular Atrophy patients
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday called for a comprehensive proposal to establish a dedicated corpus fund aimed at providing financial assistance and systematic treatment to patients suffering from Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA), a rare and debilitating genetic disorder. A Bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana stressed that individual charity and ad-hoc government grants are insufficient, and there is a pressing need for a permanent, regularised channel to finance life-saving therapies. "Depending on individual circumstances, corporate social responsibility (CSR) contributions may come forward, or the government may release grants. But what we need is a regular channel, a permanent system. There should be a mechanism for automatic contributions and a regular fund that is maintained," the CJI observed. The Court further underscored that any such mechanism must prioritise the optimum utilisation of resources on a strictly non-profit basis to ensure direct patient support. The top court was hearing suo motu proceedings initiated by it to address the lack of adequate, systematic, and affordable healthcare infrastructure for SMA

items.title: Want to change your name as per astrology, numerology? Here's what Karnataka High Court said
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently set aside a civil court's refusal to allow a minor girl to change her name, and allowed the name change opted by her and her family for astrological and numerical reasons. Justice Hanchate Sanjeevkumar added that every Indian has a civil right to be recognised by their name and that people can, therefore, approach civil courts for a name change. "Every person in society is necessarily to be recognized by his/her name. It is a civil right of every citizen in India to be recognized by his/her name. Therefore, for correction or change of name, filing a suit before the Civil Court is maintainable, as it relates to the adjudication of a civil right," the Court said. In this case, the Court also noted that changing the name change was not objected to by anyone, and that it would not cause any harm to any person. items.title: Kerala HC upholds ₹10k monthly maintenance for ex-wife of paralysed man who said he married only for a maid
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently upheld a family court order directing a man who had suffered a paralytic stroke to pay ₹10,000 per month as maintenance to his ex-wife, rejecting his defence that there were no marital relations between them and that he had married her to get a maid servant. Justice G Girish also sharply criticised the man's claim that he had married only because he wanted a maid who would take care of him and his mother. " Even as per the version of the petitioner (husband), he had adopted the deceitful tactics of making a matrimonial advertisement for the ostensible purpose of getting a servant, and succeeded in contracting a marriage with the respondent (wife) with the full knowledge that he is incapable of performing his conjugal obligations to his wife. After spoiling the life of a lady by resorting to such a dubious method, the petitioner cannot evade from his responsibility to make payment of maintenance to the respondent, " the Court said. items.title: NYAI launches NYAI AI Studio: India’s first Agentic AI Infrastructure Platform for legal and compliance
items.summary: NYAI has launched NYAI AI Studio , India’s first agentic AI infrastructure platform purpose-built for law firms and the legal and compliance functions of enterprises. The Studio marks a decisive shift from AI that assists with discrete tasks to AI agents that execute legal and compliance work end to end, from intake to delivery, on the organisation’s own data, under its own controls and through its own choice of AI models. Rather than adding yet another point solution to an already crowded legal-technology stack, NYAI AI Studio unites data, agents, models, tools, workflows, institutional knowledge and governance within a single environment, giving every organisation the infrastructure to build an AI practice in its own image. Advocate Dr. Chinmay S. Bhosale , Co-founder, NYAI, shared, “Legal and compliance teams cannot treat AI as merely another productivity application.
